Avulsion (river).fact: In sedimentary geology and fluvial geomorphology, avulsion is the process by which flow is diverted out of an set up river channel and into a new course via a bifurcation, or splitting of the channel. Battle of Puná.fact: The Battle of Puná, a peripheral engagement of Francisco Pizarro's conquest of Peru, was fought in April 1531 on the island of Puná (in the Gulf of Guayaquil) in Ecuador.

Battle of Puná.subject: World Geography
Battle of Puná.question: The battle marked the beginning of _____'s third and final expedition prior to the fall of the Inca Empire
Battle of Puná.fact: The Battle of Puná, a peripheral engagement of Francisco Pizarro's conquest of Peru, was fought in April 1531 on the island of Puná (in the Gulf of Guayaquil) in Ecuador. Pizarro's conquistadors, boasting superior weaponry and tactical skill, decisively defeated the island's indigenous inhabitants.

Battle of Puná.subject: World Geography
Battle of Puná.question: Initially, the _____ occupation of the island proceeded without bloodshed
Battle of Puná.fact: Initially, the Spanish occupation of the island proceeded without bloodshed.

Battle of Puná.subject: World Geography
Battle of Puná.question: The path to war was first triggered by _____'s native interpreters, who warned him, perhaps falsely, that several Punian chiefs had gathered to plan an insurrection
Battle of Puná.fact: The path to war was first triggered by Pizarro's native interpreters, who warned him, perhaps falsely, that several Punian chiefs had gathered to plan an insurrection. Pizarro had the chiefs captured, interrogated, and, apparently satisfied with their guilt, delivered to their traditional enemies at Tumbes where they were duly massacred by the Incas.

Battle of Puná.question: It seemed that the diminutive _____ force would surely be overwhelmed and scattered

Battle of Puná.question: Within minutes, the _____ were in full rout
